info.description:
NAICS from a description of operations, with TypeSafe Jev choosing and code deciding.

1. **classify**: `search` finds the best-matching industries with Postgres full-text search over the official Census text, then Jev picks one of only those in one call, with a fit check. `full` walks all of NAICS 2022 (1,012 industries) down the official tree (about 5 calls). `hybrid` tries `search` first and falls back to the tree walk only when search is unsure.
2. **naics**: full-text search of the Census text, or look up any code. No model call.
3. **service**: health and the eval descriptions.

**Notes.**
- Classifying calls Jev and **costs TypeSafe credits** (with no key it replays recorded answers).
- A hold is a normal 200 result: too vague, unsure, or the picked industry does not fit.
- Routes are versioned under `/v1`; the unversioned paths still work but are deprecated.
- **Auth:** every route except health and the reference export needs `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, a key from the service's `NAICS_API_KEYS`. No credential is 401; a wrong one is 403.
- Every response carries an `X-Request-ID` header: the caller's own (1-64 of `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -`), else a new one. It is on the request's log line, so a caller can correlate its logs with the service's.
info.title: jev-naics

post.description: `hybrid` **(1 Jev call, or about 7 on a fallback)** tries `search` first and falls back to `full` only when search is unsure. `search` **(1 Jev call)** runs the full-text search, then Jev picks one of the top 10 results in one call and checks each one's fit; without the search database it holds. `full` **(about 5 Jev calls)** walks the Census tree: one call per level with every kept node asked in parallel, the best 3 paths kept, then one call that picks among the finalists and checks each one's fit. `tree` is the same walk as `full` under the name the library and README use; the response's `mode` echoes whichever of the two was sent. Every mode **costs TypeSafe credits**. Code holds when the description is too vague, the pick's probability is under its bar, or the picked industry does not fit (bars in the response field descriptions).

Type a description of operations, or any words. Postgres full-text search ranks every 2022 industry by its official title, Census index entries, illustrative examples, the activities other industries' cross-references send to it, and its description, with rare words counting more. **No model call, no cost.** Use **Classify a description** with mode `search` to have Jev pick among these.

post.description: Runs `hybrid` and `full` on the description. When both pick the same code, that code is the answer with no further call (`step: agreement`). When either holds as too vague, on a malformed answer, or on a service error, it holds. Otherwise Jev picks once over every industry either method considered (their answers plus their search results or finalists, a closed set built in code), with the same probability, fit, and vagueness gates as `search` (`step: judge`). **Costs TypeSafe credits**: about 6 Jev calls, 12 on a hybrid fallback, plus 1 when judged.

post.description: An experiment beside `/assist`, which it does not change. One Jev call carries the completeness checks and a Choice over all 1,012 industries (in blocks of at most 240); a second verifies the best candidates with their full Census text (`variant`). With `lexicon` (the default) a one- or two-word text is checked when it holds a recognised term or passes the completeness checks; without it, fewer than three words returns `TOO_SHORT` with no call. **Costs TypeSafe credits**: about 40-45k input tokens per call.

post.description: Runs `hybrid` and `full` **in parallel**; the tree walk's answer is the default. It stands when the hybrid picks the same code (`step: agreement`) or holds unsure: low probability, misfit, or no match (`step: tree_only`). It goes back to the broker (`step: broker`) when the hybrid picks a different code (`hold_reason: methods_disagree`), finds the description too vague, or fails, and whenever the tree walk holds. No judge call. **Costs TypeSafe credits**: about 6 Jev calls, 12 on a hybrid fallback.

post.description: Runs `hybrid` and `full` **in parallel**. Accepted with no further call when both pick the same code (`step: agreement`) or when only the tree walk answers and the hybrid held unsure (`step: tree_only`). A hybrid that failed (malformed answer, service error) is never read as "no answer": it goes back to the broker. Anything else (a split, a lone hybrid answer, both unsure) is judged once over every industry either method considered, with `search`'s gates (`step: judge`); a judge hold, or a too-vague description, goes back to the broker (`step: broker`). **Costs TypeSafe credits**: about 6 Jev calls, 12 on a hybrid fallback, plus 1 when judged.
